searchText: I wanted to say that not necessarily we have imported the block in fork choice when the payload arrives so that it becomes a condition. <@425572898787426305> <@755590043632140352> I have a similar question regarding the above. I'm coding this for Prysm, so I will find out about this sooner or later. Consider the following scenario: - `Slot: 100, block_root: 0xA, block_hash: 0xB` - `Slot: 101, block_root: 0xC, block_hash: 0xD` I'm a proposer for slot 102 and propose at `t`. Will EL complain if I call `{parent_block_root: 0xC, head_block_hash: 0xD}` at `t-6` and then call `{parent_block_root: 0xC, head_block_hash: 0xB}` again at `t`? Do we need to update the execution API spec here for ePBS? I don't think we need to adjust anything if today this same thing can happen I dont think it can happen today right. A block can't be empty today. Block root and block hash is 1:1 The point is that today you can send inconsistent data to the engine and it's your fault. ePBS doesn't change that The CL is expected to send the right hash/root combination, just like today <@363800010518822915>, we had <@792404665068158998> over for EPF office hours, and I asked about the data in the TG research post. It seems the relays are bundling bids data and making it public off-chain. He definitely encouraged us to reach out for any type of "exotic" data regarding the protocol
